In addition to offering relevant information and specific interactivity at a glance, people use widgets, watch complications, Live Activities, and controls to personalize their devices: People configure widgets and watch complications to display details specific to their needs.
Widgets and watch complications use a special mechanism to update their content: You create a timeline of data updates and hand it to WidgetKit.
Live Activities don’t use timelines to update their content.
Instead, they use and ActivityKit push notifications you send with APNs.
Controls don’t use timelines to update their content.

Static widgets use a for the property.

To configure a static widget, provide the following information: Use modifiers to provide additional configuration details, including a display name, a description, and the families the widget supports.
For an app’s widget to appear in the widget gallery, a person must launch the app that contains the widget at least once after the app is installed.
You can use APNs and WidgetKit push notifications to update your widgets.
In order for people to be able to use your widget, it needs to be available in the widget gallery.
If your widget would normally need assets or information that takes time to generate or fetch from a server, use sample data instead.
Widgets and watch complications may show sensitive information and can be highly visible, especially on devices with an Always-On display.
To let people decide whether a widget should show sensitive data on a locked device, mark views that contain sensitive information using the modifier.
In iOS, people can configure whether to show sensitive data on the Lock Screen and during Always On.
Use WidgetKit to build widgets, controls, watch complications, and Live Activities.

System experiences that use WidgetKit as a foundation rely on a set of related frameworks and share design and functional similarities, making them great candidates for code and design component reuse.
To avoid costly changes in your app’s development process, plan your WidgetKit adoption before you create designs and write code.
When you add support for Live Activities, you need to create minimal, compact, and extended presentations that make sure your Live Activities appear correctly for each platform.
